You're working in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-wip-discord-oauth (branch feature/discord-staff-oauth, already created off latest main in /opt/nxeon, node_modules and .env symlinked from /opt/nxeon — this gives you access to REAL, LIVE Discord OAuth credentials, described below). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon directly, do NOT merge or deploy — make the changes, verify, and report back. Do NOT run `git add -A` (a documented past incident replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink) — stage specific files by name only if asked to commit (only commit if explicitly asked; leave it uncommitted otherwise). Do NOT run `npx prisma generate` or `npx prisma db push` from this worktree — it shares the SAME symlinked node_modules as the live production app; regenerating the Prisma Client here would push not-yet-live schema types into the shared client and could break the running production app. Write schema changes as text only, and read/write any new field via explicit `as any` casts, exactly like the existing Discord bridge work already does for `Ticket.discordThreadId`/`ChatConversation.discordThreadId` — follow that exact precedent (read it before you start).

## Context — what exists already (READ this code before starting, don't guess)

Nxeon (a VPS/hosting/game-server platform) just shipped a Discord support bridge, live in production right now: `lib/discord.ts` (REST client + Ed25519 interaction-signature verification), `lib/discord-bridge.ts` (mirrors tickets/live-chat into a private Discord guild, handles the reply round-trip), `lib/reply-core.ts` (`writeTicketReply`/`writeChatReply` — the shared DB-write core both the dashboard actions and the Discord webhook call), and `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts` (the signed Interactions Endpoint). Read ALL of these in full first.

**The specific gap you're closing**: today, EVERY Discord-originated reply is attributed to a single, hardcoded `discord_reply_as_user_id` setting (one specific Nxeon admin User.id) — a deliberate, explicitly-documented placeholder for when only one person (the owner) uses this. `lib/discord-bridge.ts`'s top-of-file comment says outright: *"When actual support staff join later, this is the seam to replace with real per-Discord-user identity linking — do NOT bolt that on here without designing it properly."* That moment is now. The owner wants real OAuth-based linking so that when a support-staff member (not just the owner) clicks Reply in Discord and types a message, it's correctly attributed to THEM specifically, not to one shared fake identity.

Already stored in the live encrypted-settings store (read via `getSetting`/`decryptSecret` from `lib/settings.ts`/`lib/crypto-box.ts`, same pattern as the existing `discord_bot_token`):
- `discord_application_id`, `discord_public_key`, `discord_bot_token` (encrypted), `discord_guild_id`, `discord_enabled` (currently `"true"`, live), `discord_reply_as_user_id` (currently set to the one admin's User.id).
- **New**: `discord_client_secret` (encrypted) — the OAuth2 client secret for this same Discord application. Add its getter to `lib/discord.ts` alongside the existing credential getters, following the exact same pattern (`getSetting`/`decryptSecret`, add to `SECRET_KEYS` in `lib/settings.ts` if you add a `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` entry for it — check how `discord_bot_token` was registered there and mirror it exactly).
- The registered OAuth2 redirect URI in Discord's Developer Portal is exactly: `https://nxeon.cloud/api/admin/discord/callback` — your callback route MUST live at that exact path (`app/api/admin/discord/callback/route.ts`) or Discord will reject the redirect with a mismatch error.

## What to build

### 1. Schema

Add `discordUserId String? @unique` to the `User` model (`prisma/schema.prisma`) — nullable and unique (a Discord account can only ever be linked to one Nxeon user, and a Nxeon user has at most one linked Discord account). Follow the exact same "NOT YET PUSHED to the live database" doc-comment discipline already used on `Ticket.discordThreadId` — copy that comment's structure and adapt it.

### 2. The OAuth flow

Two new routes:
- **`app/api/admin/discord/authorize/route.ts`** (or wherever fits this codebase's actual admin route conventions — check `app/admin/` and `app/api/admin/` for the existing pattern first): requires the caller to already be signed in as real Nxeon staff (use whatever this codebase's existing `requireArea("support")`/`canAccess()` pattern is — `lib/rbac.ts`, already used by `lib/actions-chat.ts`/`lib/actions-support.ts` — read it to get the exact right guard, a CUSTOMER-role user must never be able to link a Discord identity to their own account and use it for staff actions). Generates a CSRF-safe `state` value (store it however this codebase already handles short-lived server-side state — check if there's an existing pattern, e.g. a signed cookie or a short-lived DB row; if nothing existing fits cleanly, a signed, expiring value using the same HMAC/crypto primitives already in this codebase, e.g. something built on `AUTH_SECRET`, is fine — do NOT invent a new secret-management scheme when one likely already exists for something structurally similar like password-reset tokens, check `lib/actions-account.ts`'s reset-token pattern for a precedent). Redirects to Discord's OAuth2 authorize URL (`https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&scope=identify&state=...`).
- **`app/api/admin/discord/callback/route.ts`**: validates `state` (reject with a clear error if missing/expired/tampered), exchanges the `code` for an access token via `POST https://discord.com/api/v10/oauth2/token` (form-encoded body: `client_id`, `client_secret`, `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `redirect_uri` — must exactly match what was sent in the authorize step), then calls `GET https://discord.com/api/v10/users/@me` with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` to get the Discord user's real id. Writes that id onto the CURRENTLY SIGNED-IN staff user's `User.discordUserId` (re-derive who's signing in from the same session/auth mechanism used elsewhere, do NOT trust a value passed through the OAuth `state` round-trip for identity — only use `state` for CSRF protection, re-check the real session at callback time). Handle the case where that Discord user id is ALREADY linked to a DIFFERENT Nxeon user (the `@unique` constraint will throw — catch it and show a clear "this Discord account is already linked to another Nxeon staff account" error, don't let a raw Prisma constraint error leak to the user). Redirect back to wherever the admin UI (see below) lives, with a success/error indicator.
- An **unlink** action (a simple server action or route, staff-only, sets their own `discordUserId` back to null) — people should be able to disconnect and relink.

### 3. Admin UI

Find the right existing place for this — likely somewhere in the admin settings area or a staff profile page (check `app/admin/settings/` and any existing "my account"/profile page for admin/support users — read what's there first rather than inventing a new page if a sensible one already exists). Add a small "Discord account" section: shows linked status (and maybe the Discord username if easy to fetch/display), a "Connect Discord" button (links to the authorize route) when unlinked, a "Disconnect" button when linked.

### 4. Update the reply-attribution logic — the actual point of this work

This is in `lib/discord-bridge.ts`'s `submitDiscordReply` (or wherever the reply-webhook path currently reads `discord_reply_as_user_id`) and `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts`. Discord's interaction payload includes `interaction.member.user.id` (for a guild interaction — this bridge only ever operates inside one guild, so `member` will always be present, not `interaction.user` which is only for DM interactions) — this is the REAL Discord user id of whoever clicked the button/submitted the modal, sent and Ed25519-signed by Discord itself, so it's trustworthy once signature verification (already implemented) passes.

Change the reply path to:
1. Extract `interaction.member.user.id` from the verified interaction payload.
2. Look up `User.findUnique({ where: { discordUserId: thatId } })`.
3. If found AND that user actually has staff access (reuse whatever role/permission check governs ticket/chat replies elsewhere — e.g. `isSupportStaff`/`canAccess(role, "support")` from `lib/rbac.ts`, don't invent a new check), attribute the reply to THEM (their real `User.id`) via the existing `writeTicketReply`/`writeChatReply` calls.
4. If NOT found (no linked Discord account, or the linked Nxeon account doesn't have staff access — e.g. someone was demoted/removed), respond with a clear, visible message back in Discord: something like "⚠️ Your Discord account isn't linked to a Nxeon staff account. Link it at https://nxeon.cloud/admin/settings (or wherever you placed the UI) to reply from here." — never silently fail, never fall back to a fake/anonymous identity.

**Design decision for you to make and justify in your report**: should the old `discord_reply_as_user_id` setting still work as a fallback (e.g. if the resolved Discord user has no link, fall back to that one configured user instead of rejecting), or should real per-user linking now be the ONLY path, with `discord_reply_as_user_id` effectively retired? Consider: the whole point of this work is correct per-person attribution; keeping a silent fallback to one shared identity partially undermines that, but might be a reasonable transition aid for the owner's own account specifically if they haven't linked yet themselves. Pick one, document why, and if you keep a fallback, make it OPT-IN and clearly logged/visible when it's used (never a silent substitution) — not a default that quietly papers over an unlinked account. My inclination given the point of this feature is to retire the fallback and require the owner to link their own account too, but genuinely use your judgment and justify whichever you pick.

## Security constraints

- The OAuth `state` parameter MUST provide real CSRF protection — don't skip it or make it trivially guessable.
- The callback route must re-derive the real signed-in Nxeon user from the actual session at callback time, never from anything passed through the OAuth round-trip itself.
- Only real Nxeon staff (not CUSTOMER-role users) can ever initiate the linking flow or have a linked Discord identity actually usable for reply-attribution — even if a customer somehow got a `discordUserId` written (they shouldn't be able to reach the authorize route at all, but defense-in-depth: the reply-webhook's role check in step 3 above is what actually matters at reply time).
- The client secret must be read via the encrypted-settings pattern, never hardcoded, never logged.

## Test baseline

`npm test` currently has 34 pre-existing, unrelated failures (pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests) — established, known baseline. Confirm zero NEW failures beyond that same set of 34.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — must be clean.
2. `npm test` — compare against the 34-failure baseline, confirm zero new failures. Add real tests for: the state-parameter CSRF logic (a tampered/expired/missing state is rejected), the reply-attribution resolution logic (linked staff user → correct attribution; unlinked Discord id → clear rejection message, not a silent fallback unless you deliberately kept one — test whichever behavior you chose).
3. You have REAL, LIVE Discord OAuth credentials and a real guild. If you can safely test the authorize→callback round-trip against the real Discord OAuth endpoint without needing an actual browser-driven user consent click (which you can't automate), at least verify the pieces you CAN test live: that the authorize URL you construct is well-formed and Discord accepts it as a valid request shape (you can `curl` it and confirm you get a real Discord login/consent page back, not an error), and that your token-exchange code correctly handles Discord's real token-endpoint error responses (e.g. deliberately send it a bogus `code` and confirm your code parses Discord's real error response correctly rather than crashing). A full click-through consent flow needs an actual human in a browser — note clearly in your report what you could vs. couldn't verify live, matching how the original Discord-bridge build honestly reported its own live-testing limits.

## Report back

Summarize what you built, where you placed the admin UI and why, your fallback-vs-retire design decision and reasoning, confirmation of all verification steps including what you could/couldn't test live, and exactly what's needed before this goes live (schema push, and — critically — since discord_reply_as_user_id's role may change — what the owner needs to do, e.g. "link your own Discord account via the new UI before support-staff replies stop working if you retired the fallback"). Leave the change uncommitted in the worktree for review.

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "accounting"
22	  | "platform";
23	
24	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
25	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
26	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
27	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
28	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
30	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
31	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
32	  // Real cost/margin data (expenses, net income) — ADMIN only, unlike "billing"
33	  // (which BILLING-role staff also reach for day-to-day invoice/refund work).
34	  accounting: ["ADMIN"],
35	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
36	};

38	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
39	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
40	}

44	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";

141	/**
142	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
143	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
144	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).

Everything is in place, uncommitted, and verified. Here's the full report.

## What was built

**Schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): added `User.discordUserId String? @unique`, right next to the analogous `googleId` field, with the same "NOT YET pushed to the live database" doc-comment discipline as `Ticket.discordThreadId`/`ChatConversation.discordThreadId`. All reads/writes go through explicit `as any` casts, matching that exact precedent.

**OAuth protocol** (`lib/discord-oauth.ts`, new): authorize-URL builder, token exchange (`client_secret_post` to Discord's real v10 token endpoint), and `/users/@me` identify call. `discordClientSecret()` was added to `lib/discord.ts` (decrypt-on-read, same pattern as `discordBotToken()`), with `discord_client_secret` added to `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`/`SECRET_KEYS` in `lib/settings.ts`.

**CSRF `state`**: rather than cookie-stashed state (Cloudflare's pattern in `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts`), `state` is itself a short-lived signed JWT (`jose`, `AUTH_SECRET`, 10-minute expiry, a `typ: "discord_oauth_state"` claim so it can't be confused with a session/impersonation token) embedding the initiating user's id. This needs no server-side storage and is a pure, unit-testable function pair (`signDiscordOauthState`/`verifyDiscordOauthState`).

**Routes**: `app/api/admin/discord/authorize/route.ts` (gated `requireArea("support")`, mints state, redirects to Discord) and `app/api/admin/discord/callback/route.ts` at the exact registered path. The callback re-derives the real user via `requireArea("support")` independently of anything in the OAuth round-trip; `state`'s subject is used only to *check equality* against that real user, never as a write target. A `P2002` unique-conflict on `discordUserId` is caught and surfaced as "already linked to another Nxeon staff account."

**Unlink**: `lib/actions-discord-link.ts` — `getDiscordLinkStatus()` and `disconnectDiscordLink()`, both `requireArea("support")`-gated server actions.

**UI**: `components/admin/DiscordIntegration.tsx`, wired into `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx`'s existing "Integrations" tab (which already hosts `CloudflareIntegration` and `ClaudeKeyConnect` — this page is the established shared account-settings surface used by both customers and staff, not the ADMIN-only `/admin/settings`). Visibility is gated on `canAccess(role, "support")` so BILLING/CUSTOMER accounts never see a button that could never do anything for them.

**Attribution rework** (`lib/discord-bridge.ts`): `extractInteractionUserId` (new, `lib/discord.ts`) pulls the real, Discord-signed `interaction.member.user.id`. `resolveDiscordReplyActor` (new, pure function) resolves it against `User.findUnique({ where: { discordUserId } })` and requires `canAccess(role, "support")`. `submitDiscordReply` now takes that id as a parameter; `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts` passes it through.

## Design decision: fallback retired, not kept

No fallback to `discord_reply_as_user_id`. An unlinked or since-demoted Discord account gets a visible, specific Discord message ("link your account at .../dashboard/settings?tab=integrations") instead of ever silently reattributing to a shared identity. Rationale: the whole point of this work is correct per-person attribution, and a silent shared-identity fallback (even opt-in) undermines that for the one case it would most often mask — someone forgetting to link. The cost is real and immediate: **the owner's own Discord replies will stop working the moment this ships, until the owner links their own account through the new Settings UI.** `discord_reply_as_user_id` is marked retired in code comments, no longer read anywhere, kept only as a historical record.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npm test`: 1317 tests, 34 failing — identical set to the documented pre-existing baseline (pricing/proration/auth-baseline), confirmed by name. Zero new failures.
- New tests, all passing: `test/discord-oauth-state.test.ts` (real `jose` sign/verify — valid, wrong-uid, missing, tampered signature, forged-secret, expired, wrong-`typ`, garbage), `test/discord-reply-attribution.test.ts` (linked staff → correct attribution; unlinked/demoted → rejection, never a fallback; `extractInteractionUserId` shape handling), `test/discord-oauth-guards.test.ts` (source-tripwire style, matching this repo's established discipline of not importing route modules that would open a live DB connection — verifies the staff gate precedes state-minting/param-reads, and that the DB write is keyed on `me.id` from the real session, never on anything from `state`).
- **Live verification against real Discord**: `discord_client_secret` was already present in the live encrypted `Setting` table (owner had pre-provisioned it). Confirmed live: (1) the built authorize URL is well-formed and Discord returns a real 200 consent-app response; (2) a real POST to Discord's token endpoint with a deliberately wrong `client_secret` returns `invalid_client` (401), while the *real* decrypted secret + a bogus `code` instead returns Discord's real `invalid_grant` / `Invalid "code" in request.` — proving the stored `client_id`/`client_secret` pair is genuinely valid and `discordExchangeCode` correctly builds the request and parses Discord's real error shape without crashing. **Not verified live**: a full human consent click-through (needs a browser) and definitive redirect-URI-mismatch behavior specifically (Discord validates the authorization code before redirect_uri on this error path, so a bogus code masks that check either way).

## Before this goes live

1. Real `npx prisma db push` + `prisma generate` for `User.discordUserId` (not run here, per instructions — shared prod `node_modules`).
2. The owner must link their own Discord account via Settings → Integrations before promoting, or their own Discord replies stop working immediately (no fallback).
3. Confirm `https://nxeon.cloud/api/admin/discord/callback` is the exact registered redirect URI in the Discord Developer Portal (per the task spec, it already is).
